template_name: Fabrication of Ni-5at%W substrates with CeO2/YSZ/Y2O3 buffer layers
description: Ni-5at%W alloy substrates were selected for their high mechanical strength and ability to develop strong cube texture through rolling/annealing processes.
CeO2/YSZ/Y2O3 multilayer buffer structure was deposited via sputtering to prevent Ni diffusion, transfer substrate texture, and provide lattice matching for YBCO growth.
application_scenarios: For REBCO superconducting layers requiring biaxial texture
For coated conductors needing diffusion barriers
For applications demanding high critical current density
reason_flow: Step 1: Substrate preparation - Cold rolling with 95% reduction followed by recrystallization annealing at 1000°C in forming gas to achieve cube texture {surface roughness <5nm}
Step 2: Buffer layer deposition - Sequential sputtering of CeO2 (20nm), YSZ (50nm), Y2O3 (30nm) at 700°C with 0.5Pa Ar/O2 mixture {maintain Δa <0.5% between layers}
Step 3: Interface optimization - Post-deposition annealing at 850°C in vacuum to enhance crystallinity and reduce mismatch stress {FWHM <3° in φ-scan}

example_application.example_problem: How to fabricate a 100m-long coated conductor with Jc >1MA/cm² at 77K
solution_process: Step 1: Prepare Ni-5at%W tape through 12-pass rolling with 8% reduction per pass
Step 2: Anneal at 1000°C for 2hrs in 4%H2/Ar atmosphere to develop cube texture
Step 3: Deposit CeO2 layer by DC sputtering at 700°C with 150W power and 0.3Pa pressure
Step 4: Grow YSZ layer using RF sputtering at 750°C with 200W power and 0.4Pa pressure
Step 5: Deposit Y2O3 cap layer by pulsed laser deposition at 800°C with 5Hz repetition rate
Answer: {Achieved Jc=1.2MA/cm² at 77K with Δφ=2.8° and surface roughness Ra=3.2nm}

template_name: Preparation of Ni-5at%W substrates and CeO2/YSZ/Y2O3 buffer layers
description: Ni-5at%W alloy substrates were selected for their non-magnetic properties, mechanical strength, and ability to develop strong cube texture through rolling/recrystallization.

A triple-layer CeO2/YSZ/Y2O3 buffer architecture was deposited via sputtering to prevent Ni diffusion, transfer substrate texture, and match thermal expansion coefficients with superconducting layers.
application_scenarios: For REBCO superconducting tapes requiring biaxial texture
For high critical current density applications
reason_flow: Step 1: Substrate preparation through cold rolling (95% reduction) and annealing (900-1100°C in Ar-4%H2) to achieve cube texture
Step 2: Y2O3 seed layer deposition by reactive sputtering (400°C, 5e-3 Torr) to initiate aligned growth
Step 3: YSZ barrier layer formation (DC sputtering at 650°C) for diffusion blocking
Step 4: CeO2 cap layer deposition (RF sputtering at 750°C) for surface planarization
Step 5: Thermal treatment optimization (800°C annealing) to enhance layer crystallinity and interface quality

example_application.example_problem: How to achieve high-quality buffer layers on textured Ni-W substrates for coated conductors?
solution_process: Step 1: Prepare Ni-5at%W substrate with 95% cold rolling reduction and anneal at 1000°C for 1h in reducing atmosphere
Step 2: Deposit 50nm Y2O3 seed layer via reactive sputtering at 400°C with 10sccm oxygen flow
Step 3: Grow 200nm YSZ layer by DC sputtering at 650°C with 5e-3 Torr working pressure
Step 4: Deposit 100nm CeO2 cap layer using RF sputtering at 750°C and 2e-2 Torr
Step 5: Perform post-annealing at 800°C for 30min in Ar/H2 mixture
Answer: {Achieved buffer layers with Δφ < 5° in-plane texture, surface roughness <5nm RMS, and critical current density >3MA/cm² at 77K}

template_name: Ni-W alloy substrate preparation with Y2O3 buffer layer deposition
description: Ni-5at%W alloy substrates were developed for their improved mechanical strength and non-magnetic properties compared to pure nickel. Y2O3 buffer layers were deposited to prevent nickel diffusion and provide lattice matching for subsequent superconducting layer growth.
application_scenarios: For REBCO-type superconducting layers requiring biaxial texture
For applications demanding high critical current density
reason_flow: Step 1: Substrate fabrication - Cold rolling with 95% reduction followed by recrystallization annealing at 800-1000°C in forming gas atmosphere to develop cube texture
Step 2: Surface treatment - Electro-polishing in H3PO4:CH3COOH (2:1) solution to achieve surface roughness <5nm
Step 3: Buffer layer deposition - Pulsed laser deposition of Y2O3 at 800°C with oxygen partial pressure 1e-2 Torr to obtain 50nm thick layer
Step 4: Structural optimization - Maintaining lattice mismatch <5% between substrate and buffer layer through precise thickness control

example_application.example_problem: How to achieve high-quality YBCO growth on metallic substrates with minimized interface diffusion
solution_process: Step 1: Prepare Ni-5at%W alloy through vacuum induction melting and homogenization at 1200°C for 24h
Step 2: Cold roll to 0.1mm thickness with 95% total reduction ratio
Step 3: Recrystallization anneal at 850°C in Ar-4%H2 atmosphere for 1h
Step 4: Deposit 50nm Y2O3 layer by PLD at 800°C with laser energy density 2J/cm²
Step 5: Characterize using XRD ω-scan showing FWHM <5° for (200) reflection
Answer: {Achieved YBCO films with Jc >1MA/cm² at 77K through optimized substrate/buffer architecture}
